title: Model anchoring: routing controls, region affinity, and compatibility notes (wip)
body:
Purpose and scope

This is a working note capturing the 'anchoring' (a.k.a. pinning) semantics we want between the model registry and the global routing/control plane, with a focus on multi-region affinity and predictable fallbacks. Goal: create deterministic, observable behavior that is simple for customers to reason about and cheap to operate.

Why "anchoring"?
- 'Pinning' has been used inconsistently: sometimes meaning tenant-level hard pin, sometimes meaning soft preference. 'Anchoring' intentionally implies a preferred binding plus explicit fallback rules and provenance metadata.

Surface requirements / design goals
- Deterministic routing decisions for a request given: tenant config (anchor), runtime availability, region cost/latency policy, and compatibility (model architecture / quantization).
- Minimal per-request compute in the control plane (cacheable routing decisions, TTLs).
- Strong telemetry: why a particular model/version was chosen (anchor match, fallback reason, compatibility scoring).
- Clear semantics for canary/rollouts and temporary overrides (urgent hotfixes).
- Safe fallbacks: preserve privacy/tenant isolation guarantees and avoid routing to lower-tier hardware unintentionally.

Key concepts (short)
- Anchor: authoritative registry entry binding: {model-id, version-id, anchor-type}. Anchor-types: hard, soft, capacity-affinity, region-affinity.
- Compatibility profile: per-version metadata describing required runtime capabilities (min-kernel, required-quant, kv-cache-behavior, memory-footprint-band).
- Routing policy: set of weighted/priority rules in control plane (latencySLO-first, cost-first, dedicated-only).
- Region affinity: explicit region preference list attached to an anchor (r1, r2, fallback-global).

Compatibility scoring (sketch)
We need a simple ordinal score (0..100) computed in control plane to compare candidate model variants. Score components:
- Runtime match (0/1): does target compute flavor support required kernel/quant? (binary).
- Latency delta penalty (0..30): estimated p95 delta vs anchor region baseline.
- Cost delta penalty (0..30): normalized per-token cost delta.
- Isolation penalty (0..20): penalize if candidate is in shared pool vs dedicated anchor.
- Freshness bonus (0..20): prefer same or newer version within compatible family.
FinalScore = runtime_match * (100 - sum(penalties) + freshness_bonus). Non-match on runtime_match => score 0 (incompatible).

Example: anchor is model-x v3 (dedicated in eu-west). Candidate: model-x v2 in global-shared, runtime match yes, latency +25ms => latency penalty 10, cost +0.6c => cost penalty 12, isolation penalty 20, freshness bonus 0 => final ~58 => fallback allowed but deprioritized.

Policy modes and semantics
- Hard anchor: routing must only return the exact (model-id, version-id) instances in specified region(s); if unavailable, request fails or uses explicit emergency fallback route (operator-approved). Use-case: regulated customers or experiments requiring bit-exact models.
- Soft anchor: preferred model/version; control plane will consult compatibility scoring and routing policy to decide fallbacks. Soft anchors can have TTLs and automated roll-forward behavior.
- Capacity-affinity anchor: anchor expresses preference for capacity-type (dedicated vs shared) rather than explicit version; used for teams that care about throughput not exact model.
- Region-affinity anchor: anchor expresses region list; within list, ranking by compatibility score.

Rollouts and canaries
- Canary anchoring: attach an anchor tag to a small % of traffic. Control plane must evaluate per-request whether to route to canary variant (deterministic hashing on request id + tenant id).
- Gradual roll: increment % by config change. If compatibility regressions are detected in eval telemetry (per-prompt score drop, increased hallucination rate), automatically pause or rollback.

Cache and control-plane performance
- Cache key: tenant + route + anchor_hash + client_region_hint + policy_hash. TTL 30s default, configurable per-tenant.
- Telemetry: cache-miss ratio, average decision latency, per-decision provenance (anchor-match|fallback|compatibility-score). These must be included in request traces to aid SRE.

Telemetry fields (proposed)
- routing.provenance: one of [anchor_exact, anchor_region_fallback, compatibility_fallback, policy_forced, hard_anchor_blocked]
- routing.selected: model-id@version-id
- routing.score: numeric
- routing.reason: short text (e.g., "dedicated-unavailable, runtime-incompatible, increased-latency")
- routing.decision_latency_ms

Operational play: common scenarios and suggested responses
1) Anchor pinned to version that is retired from runtime (kernel removed)
   - Detection: routing.score == 0 + telemetry reason runtime-incompatible. Alert INF-1284.
   - Response: auto-notify owning team, suggest next-compatible version from registry suggestions (see registry API: /model/{id}/compat).
2) Regional outage making anchor unavailable
   - Hard anchor: escalate to oncall, option to enable emergency fallback (operator-only).
   - Soft anchor: control plane should route to highest-score candidate and mark tenant as degraded in UI.
3) Silent quality regression after automated rollout
   - Trigger: quality monitor detects eval set regression > threshold.
   - Response: auto-pause rollout by reverting routing percentage or switch anchor back to stable version.

Compatibility matrix (authoritative source)
- We maintain a registry-provided CSV per model family: columns [version, required_kernel, min_cuda_sm, quant_supports, kvcache_behavior, memory_gb_band]
- Control plane keeps an indexed copy and recomputes scores when runtime inventory changes.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes for discussion)
- Should soft anchors support time-based automatic roll-forward (e.g., prefer newest compatible after 30d)? Pros: reduces maintenance. Cons: surprises customers. Consider opt-in per-tenant.
- Where to store per-tenant anchor TTLs and overrides? Control plane config store vs registry entry. Tradeoffs: locality vs single source of truth.
- Attack surface: malicious tenant could craft anchors to force expensive routing (dedicated) for denial-of-cost attacks. Need quota/cost caps and policy checks.
- Will we allow cross-family fallbacks (e.g., smaller-distilled model) automatically? Probably only with explicit tenant opt-in and compatibility threshold.

Implementation sketch / next steps
- Short-term (2 sprints):
  - Add "anchor-type" and "region_affinity" fields to registry API (PR linked).
  - Implement compatibility-score function in control plane prototype.
  - Add basic telemetry fields to routing decision trace.
- Mid-term (1 quarter):
  - Rollout soft-anchor with per-tenant opt-in and UI in Console (status + degrade badge).
  - Implement operator emergency-fallback workflow and audit log.
- Long-term: auto-suggestions in registry for nearest-compatible version + integration with Optimize recommendations.

Notes / loose references
- See ticket INF-1284 for recent runtime-incompat example (eu-west kernel change).
- Slack thread #plat-routing-anchors (link pinned in ticket) has discussion on hard vs soft semantics.

Appendix: small worked example
- Tenant: finance-prod, anchor: model-bert-large v7, anchor-type: soft, region_affinity: [eu-west, us-east]
- Request from eu-west user during eu-west GPU maintenance (only global shared avail):
  - Control plane reads anchor, fetches candidates; v7 runtime match false (new kernel removed), v6 runtime match true (shared only) => v6 score 72 => routed to v6, telemetry.routing.provenance=compatibility_fallback, UI shows degraded state.

Unresolved actions (owner: Priya)
- Draft registry schema change and share with registry and serving-runtime teams (due 2024-11-20).
- Prototype score function + test harness with simulated runtime inventory (due 2024-12-10).

Questions for the group
- Are there regulatory constraints that force 'hard anchor' semantics outside tenant opt-in? (Lina to check with legal).
- Do we want a separate billing signal when fallback moves a tenant from dedicated -> shared? (Finance input needed).

End of note. This is intentionally informal; please comment inline.
